title: Document Intelligence (IDP)
shortDefinition: AI technology that extracts structured, usable data from unstructured or semi-structured documents.
definition: Document Intelligence, also called Intelligent Document Processing (IDP), is AI technology that extracts structured, usable data from unstructured or semi-structured documents — invoices, contracts, forms, receipts — combining text extraction, layout understanding, and entity recognition to turn document content into data your systems can actually use. IDP goes beyond basic text extraction by understanding document structure: which numbers are line items, which date is the due date, which field is the total amount.

sections.title: How document intelligence goes beyond basic OCR
sections.description: OCR converts text to machine-readable format; IDP understands structure and meaning.

content.text: Basic OCR (optical character recognition) converts an image of text into machine-readable text, but doesn't understand what that text means or how it's structured. Document intelligence builds on top of OCR with layout analysis (understanding tables, headers, and form fields) and entity extraction (identifying that a specific number is the invoice total, not just any number on the page), producing structured, labeled data rather than an undifferentiated block of extracted text. This structural understanding is what makes IDP genuinely useful for automating document-heavy business processes.

content.title: The key insight
content.text: OCR gives you text. IDP gives you data — structured, labeled, and ready for your business systems.

IDP powers invoice processing (extracting vendor, line items, totals, and due dates for accounts payable automation), contract analysis (identifying key clauses, dates, and parties), claims processing (extracting structured data from insurance claim forms and supporting documents), and form processing (converting completed paper or PDF forms into structured database entries). The common thread is replacing manual data entry from documents with automated, accurate extraction at scale.

sections.title: Limitations and risks of document intelligence

content.text: Document intelligence has limitations. Poor quality scans or images can significantly reduce OCR and layout accuracy. Highly complex document layouts (multiple tables, nested sections) are challenging, and IDP models trained on one document type or format often don't transfer well to others. Handwritten text has variable accuracy, and confidence scoring, while helpful, requires clear thresholds and human review processes. Document processing requires ongoing maintenance as document formats and vendors change.

items: Image quality: poor scans reduce OCR and layout accuracy.
Complex layouts: nested tables and sections are challenging.
Format diversity: models often don't transfer well across document types.
Handwriting: variable and often lower accuracy than printed text.
Confidence threshold: requires careful tuning and human review processes.
Maintenance: ongoing updates needed as document formats and vendors change.
Training data: requires representative samples of your document variety.

content.title: Important
content.text: IDP systems require careful validation on your actual document types. A model that works on one set of invoices may fail on a different vendor's format.

sections.title: Best practices for document intelligence implementation

content.text: Building effective document intelligence requires careful document type definition, training data quality, and validation. The following practices can help ensure your IDP system delivers reliable extraction.

content.title: Recommended approach:
items: Define your document types and extraction fields clearly before building.
Collect a representative sample covering your document variety.
Use high-quality scans or images to maximize OCR accuracy.
Tune confidence thresholds and set up human review processes.
Validate extraction accuracy on a held-out sample of real documents.
Monitor extraction accuracy over time and retrain as needed.
Plan for ongoing maintenance as document formats and vendors change.
Integrate structured output directly into your business systems.

content.title: Key metric
content.text: Measure field-level extraction accuracy on your actual document types — overall document accuracy often masks specific fields that consistently fail.

faqs.title: Frequently asked questions about document intelligence

items.question: What's the difference between OCR and document intelligence/IDP?
items.answer: OCR converts an image of text into machine-readable text; IDP builds on top of that with layout understanding and entity extraction, producing structured, labeled data rather than just raw extracted text.

items.question: Can IDP handle handwritten documents?
items.answer: With varying accuracy depending on handwriting clarity; ClickMasters validates this specifically against samples of your actual handwritten documents if relevant to your use case.

items.question: How accurate is document intelligence extraction?
items.answer: This varies significantly by document quality and complexity; ClickMasters provides a measured accuracy figure specific to your document types rather than a generic claim.

items.question: Can IDP integrate with our existing accounting or ERP system?
items.answer: Yes, ClickMasters builds extraction pipelines that feed structured data directly into your existing accounting, ERP, or document management systems.

items.question: How long does a document intelligence project take?
items.answer: 8–24 weeks depending on document type diversity and system integration requirements.

items.question: Can IDP handle multiple languages in our document set?
items.answer: Yes, with appropriate multilingual OCR and entity extraction models; ClickMasters scopes language requirements during Discovery.

items.question: What are the most common document types processed by IDP?
items.answer: The most common document types are invoices, purchase orders, receipts, contracts, insurance claim forms, loan applications, and medical records. ClickMasters specializes in custom tuning for your specific document types.

items.question: How do you handle low-quality or scanned documents in IDP?
items.answer: Pre-processing techniques like deskewing, denoising, and contrast enhancement can improve OCR quality. For consistently poor-quality documents, ClickMasters may recommend process improvements at the scanning stage.

items.question: What is the difference between IDP and RPA for document processing?
items.answer: RPA (Robotic Process Automation) can automate data entry by mimicking human keystrokes but struggles with unstructured data. IDP uses AI to understand document structure and extract meaning, making it much more capable for complex documents.

items.question: How do you maintain IDP accuracy as document formats change?
items.answer: Document formats evolve as vendors update their templates. ClickMasters builds monitoring to detect accuracy drift and schedules periodic reviews to update extraction models when significant format changes occur.
